descs: Fallow ground, gone to reed and rush, forty years untended.

spots.name: Cold Hearth Row
spots.desc: A row of cottages, doors long fallen in, hearths cold enough that moss has taken every one of them. A dike-worker's billhook leans forgotten against the last threshold, its edge kept sharp by rust rather than care.
spots.brief: Cold cottages, a billhook left leaning.

spots.name: The Fallow Verge
spots.desc: The ground rises north toward a crossroads and its stone cross, the nearest thing to a living place this field has. South and every other way, fallow ground runs on past easy counting.

spots.name: The Sheep Walk
spots.desc: A worn path shows where sheep once went to water and back, twice a day, for longer than anyone living remembers. Nothing walks it now but whatever the wind moves.

actions.label: count how many kept this path last
fx: One set of wear, not three or four: whoever grazed here last had already lost every neighbor who once shared this path with them.

spots.name: Beggar's Stile
spots.desc: A stone stile marks an old boundary that means nothing to anyone left to cross it. Someone has propped a second, smaller stone beside it, unexplained.

actions.label: look closely at the second stone
fx: No boundary mark at all: a name, badly cut by an unpracticed hand, for someone who had nothing else to leave them.

spots.name: The Drowned Lane
spots.desc: A sunken cart-lane, ankle-deep in standing water even in dry weather. Marsh-mallow grows thick along both verges, and someone has pinched a few stalks recently, carefully, leaving the rest to seed.

spots.name: Nettle Court
spots.desc: A hamlet of six houses, all standing, all empty, all thick with nettle to the sill. Whoever left last shut every door behind them, out of habit more than hope.

actions.label: search the nearest shut house
fx: A tin box behind a loose hearthstone, coins still in it. Someone meant to come back for more than the nettle got to keep.
Dust, a fallen chair, nothing worth the door being shut over. Whatever this house kept, it isn't here.

spots.name: The Market Cross
spots.desc: A market cross stands at the meeting of four cart-tracks, its steps swept bare by wind rather than trade. West, Nettle Court's chimneys show through the damp; east, a barn has folded in on itself entirely.
spots.brief: A market cross. No market left to hold.

actions.label: stand where the market used to be
fx: Surveyor Pell's stakes glint pale in every field from here. The Crown has decided what this ground is for.
A recruit's boots have worn a fresh path past the cross, out toward the barn. That trade, at least, is brisk.
A returner's cart stood here this morning, gone again by noon. Someone is using this crossing again, finally.
Nobody stakes this ground, nobody drills it. The steps stay swept by wind alone, same as they've been for years.
No market, no trade, nothing decided yet about what this crossing is for. The steps stay swept by wind alone.

spots.name: Hollow Barn Field
spots.desc: A barn has folded in on its own roof-beam, timbers stacked like a cairn nobody meant to build. Rope still hangs from what was a hay-loft, frayed to a thread at its end.
spots.brief: A collapsed barn, rope still hanging.

actions.label: climb the hayloft rope (1hp on fail)
fx: The loft still holds a strongbox nobody came back to claim, its lock long since rusted through.
The rope gives a foot from the top, and you land hard on the old stalls below.

spots.name: The Mill Race
spots.desc: A dry mill-race runs east, weed-choked, toward the low grind of a wheel that shouldn't still be turning and isn't quite still either. The sound carries further than it has any right to.
spots.brief: A dry race. East: a mill's low sound.

actions.label: wade toward the sound (1hp on fail)
fx: The race is drier than it looks until it isn't. You come up on the far side with wet boots and two coins someone dropped chasing the same sound before you.
The weed-choked bed gives out from under you a stride from the wheel, and you go down hard on old stone.

spots.name: Longacre Rise
spots.desc: The ground climbs slightly toward a stand of yew. East, past the field's true edge, a smaller chapel roof shows whole against the sky — whole, and entirely unattended.
spots.brief: Rising ground. East: a second chapel.

spots.name: The Barrow Marches
spots.desc: The fallow ground gives way west to older, harder land that was never farmed at all. A single standing stone marks the border, and past it, low against the horizon, a mound predates every furrow in sight.

actions.label: puzzle out the standing stone (wits)
fx: Older than any furrow, older maybe than the barrow past it. Whatever it once marked, it wasn't a farm's edge.
The cuts are too old and too worn. Whatever this stone once said, it isn't saying it to you today.

spots.name: Sump's Edge
spots.desc: The ground goes soft and dark east of here, swallowed by a sunken patch nothing solid crosses. A roofline shows past it regardless, a hut standing on whatever firm ground the sump left alone.
spots.brief: Sunk ground. East: a hut beyond it.

actions.label: reach into the sump for the glint (1hp)
fx: A dropped coin-purse, silted but intact. You come up with it before the sump decides to keep your arm too.
The mud has a grip of its own, and it does not let go easily. You come back with a bruise and nothing else.

spots.name: The Drill Ground Verge
spots.desc: The ground softens and sinks just south, too wet to trust a boot on. Past it, out of sight, a raised voice keeps count of something — a drill, or a toll, or both.
spots.brief: Sunk ground. South: a raised voice.

actions.label: listen to the voice on the wet ground
fx: The voice is gone. Whatever counted cadence out here, nobody's answering it anymore.
The voice still counts, steadier now, unhurried. Nobody out there is being pressed to it.
The voice counts sharper than it used to, and you know exactly why.
A raised voice keeps count of something, same as it has every day since you first heard it.

spots.name: Aldergate Mill
spots.desc: A mill with its wheel still: not stopped, not silent — still there, turning slow and sure on water that should have long since silted its race shut. Nobody has ground grain here in forty years. Something keeps it moving anyway.
spots.brief: A mill, its wheel still turning.

actions.label: watch the wheel turn (1hp on fail)
fx: No water drives it, no grain waits for it. It turns because forty years of nobody stopping it never gave it a reason to.
The wheel's rhythm gets under your skin faster than you'd like, and you step back a good deal less steady.

spots.name: The East Bank
spots.desc: A shallow dike-bank marks the fallow ground's true edge, water on the far side of it dark and unhurried. Nothing moves out there worth naming, most days.
onEnterOnce: This is the Fallows: a hold that emptied in one winter forty years gone, when its people lost the will to stand and lay down in their own fields. A few dozen live here again now, at a crossroads called Wickstead.

spots.name: Sunken Croft
spots.desc: A second emptied hamlet, smaller than Nettle Court, its well capped with a flat stone someone troubled to fit exactly. Whoever did it meant the water kept clean for a return that never came.

actions.label: lift the well's fitted cap (1hp on fail)
fx: Whoever fit that stone so carefully left something below it worth the trouble: a few coins, dropped for luck or safekeeping.
The stone slips before you're ready for the weight of it, and it catches your hand on the way down.

spots.name: The Long Hedgerow
spots.desc: A hedgerow gone wild and tall enough to lose a person, threading the field in a line that once marked somebody's careful boundary. Blackthorn has claimed most of it for itself.

actions.label: force a way through the thorn (1hp)
fx: You find the one gap the thorns haven't quite closed, and come through with your skin mostly your own.
The blackthorn does not care for careful, and takes its due before you're through the other side.

spots.name: Widow's Acre
spots.desc: A single homestead, roof mostly sound, garden gone to riot. Something in the tangle is still unmistakably corn, self-seeded and stubborn, forty years past anyone planting it on purpose.
spots.brief: One homestead. Wild corn in the garden.

spots.name: The Toll Stone
spots.desc: An old boundary stone, its carved toll-rates long since meaningless, one line freshly re-cut over the weathered original: a Crown mark, recent, and not yet answered by anyone else's mark beside it.

actions.label: read the fresh-cut mark
fx: A second mark answers the first now: the Crown's claim, countersigned and made official.
A crude brand is cut crossways over the old rate-lines: the Companies' answer to whoever asks.
Plain initials are scratched in beside the Crown's mark, stubborn and unofficial and not going anywhere.
The fresh mark has been chiselled out and smoothed over. Nobody is claiming this stone, or the ground past it.
A Crown mark, recent, and not yet answered by anyone else's mark beside it.

spots.name: Reed Corner
spots.desc: Reed has crept in from whatever fen lies beyond the region's edge, closing over what was cropland one patient season at a time. It will have the whole field back, eventually, if nobody stops it.
spots.brief: Reed, creeping in from the fen.

spots.name: The Scarecrow Line
spots.desc: A row of scarecrows stands at drunken angles, straw long since spilled from most of them, one still upright enough to hold its shape against the sky at dusk.

actions.label: search the one still standing
fx: Someone stuffed more than straw into this one: a few coins, sewn into the sacking where crows wouldn't think to look.

spots.name: Dovecote Fallen
spots.desc: A dovecote lies on its side, its hundred nesting-holes empty and dark, whatever birds once kept it long since gone to wilder roosts. Nobody has righted it, though it would not take much.

actions.label: right the fallen dovecote
fx: It takes both arms and a bad angle, but it goes back up. Whether anything ever roosts in it again isn't yours to decide.

spots.name: The Chalk Pit
spots.desc: An old chalk quarry, walls gone soft and green, floor pooled with water the color of milk. Tool-marks still show near the top, abandoned mid-cut like the diggers meant to come back the following week.

spots.name: The Lightning Oak
spots.desc: A single oak, split clean down its trunk by some old strike, has kept growing anyway, half of it green and half of it bare bone-white wood. People used to leave small things wedged in the split. Some still do.

actions.label: search the split in the oak
fx: Among the coins and ribbons wedged into the living half, one carved token, older than the rest and worn nearly smooth.

spots.name: The Last Dike
spots.desc: A second dike, lower and older than the one at Hollowbrook, marks the fallow ground's furthest reach before the land gives way properly to fen. Whatever built it is long past caring whether it holds.

actions.label: cross the crumbling dike-top (1hp)
fx: A stash tucked into the old stonework, missed by whoever built this dike and everyone since.
The stonework gives without warning, and you go down into cold water up to the knee.

spots.name: The Bone Road
spots.desc: A straight track runs south, worn by forty years of the same short, grim errand. Nobody in Wickstead calls it by a kinder name than the one it earned the first winter. East, the headland, and the furrow past it.

spots.name: The Furrow's Headland
spots.desc: The Bone Road ends at a headland of raised earth, longer than any grave has a right to be, marked end to end with weathered stakes and stone — some carved, most only scratched, all of them leaning. South, the ground drops toward the furrow itself.
spots.brief: The headland. South: the long furrow.

actions.label: read the furrow markers (wits)
fx: Most of the marks have weathered to guesswork, but enough hold: a name here, a trade there, a child's height scratched beside a parent's. You piece together what the roll and Ede's memory cannot cover.
The weathering has beaten most of these past reading. It can be tried again, in better light or with better eyes.

actions.label: read the markers outright
fx: Weathered cuts are still cuts, and you have read worse. The names come up out of the stone almost as fast as you can find them, a whole headland's worth of grief made legible again.

spots.name: Marker Field
spots.desc: Smaller cairns scatter the ground east of the headland proper, each too small to hold what the long furrow holds, each still someone's. Some are recent enough that the stones haven't settled yet.

spots.name: The Southern Dikes
spots.desc: Low earthworks run on toward country the fallow fields don't claim, fen showing pale through the last of the reed. Whichever hold lies past it is somebody else's grief to carry.
onEnterOnce: This is the Fallows: a hold that emptied in one winter forty years gone, when its people lost the will to stand and lay down in their own fields. A few dozen live here again now, at a crossroads called Wickstead.

actions.label: look toward what holds the line south
fx: The earthworks keep running after the reed gives out, raised by hands with a different grief to answer than the Fallows'. Nobody here has walked that line in years.

onEnter: Something rises out of the reed where nothing was standing a moment ago — upright, unhurried, and not remotely alive.

vars.NAME: Longacre Chapel
vars.SIGN: The porch bell still hangs, its rope rotted to nothing.

vars.NAME: the Forebarrow
vars.SIGN: The turf here has never once been broken by a plow — this mound is older than the hold that grew up around it.

vars.NAME: the Picker's Hut
vars.SIGN: Sacks by the door are stacked with things nobody living remembers owning.
vars.VOICE: Nobody living comes here. So you're lost, or wanting.

vars.NAME: the Sump Camp
vars.SIGN: Tents are pitched in a neat ring, well clear of the soft ground.

fl_billhook.name: a dike-worker's billhook
fl_billhook.hint: heavy, hooked, kept sharp by rust more than care

fl_marsh_salve.name: a tin of marsh-mallow salve
fl_marsh_salve.hint: eases a wound, root and all

fx: Cool going on, and the ache underneath it eases before the tin's half empty.

fl_lost_purse.name: a drawstring purse, still tied
fl_lost_purse.hint: someone's, once; a little coin left inside

fx: Whoever tied it off meant to come back for it. The coin spends the same regardless.

fl_yew_ribbon.name: a weather-faded ribbon
fl_yew_ribbon.hint: tied low on the yew, more recent than the rest of this ground

fl_drowned_boot.name: a single waterlogged boot
fl_drowned_boot.hint: no pair anywhere near it; not worth much but the finding of it

fl_mourning_scrap.name: a scrap of black mourning-cloth
fl_mourning_scrap.hint: snagged on a bramble, dropped by someone walking this road for the same reason you are

fl_oak_token.name: a carved wooden token
fl_oak_token.hint: worn nearly smooth, wedged in the split long before you found it

fl_sheep_bell.name: a rusted sheep-bell
fl_sheep_bell.hint: the clapper still swings; nothing answers it now

fl_bank_line.name: a length of waxed fishing line, still hooked
fl_bank_line.hint: somebody meant to come back for this catch

fl_forebarrow_castoff.name: a corroded pair of shears
fl_forebarrow_castoff.hint: dropped by someone who came this far into the older dark and no further

fl_chapel_petra.name: Petra
fl_chapel_petra.desc: A Wickstead woman with a candle-stub she never lights, sitting where the porch step is worn smoothest.

topics.label: who keeps the porch now
topics.say: Petra. My grandmother swore this bell rang the fever in, not out. I still can't decide if that's why I keep coming, or despite it.

topics.label: ask what the chapel still owes
topics.say: Nothing owed, or nothing collected. Whatever's past that door, none of us has gone in to settle it in longer than I've been alive.

topics.label: count the wear before the door
topics.say: You read the wear in the stone like a trail: one set of feet, always the same size, always stopping at the same flagstone. Never past it.

fl_forebarrow_alder.name: Alder
fl_forebarrow_alder.desc: An old boundary-watcher, keeping well back from the doorstone, close enough only to be sure it's still shut.

topics.label: who minds the old stones
topics.say: Alder. I mind the old boundary-stones, for what little that's worth. This mound was old when the ones your Furrow keeps were still standing.

topics.label: ask what this ground is owed
topics.say: Older debts than the Fallows can pay, is my guess. Whatever's inside, it isn't waiting on us to settle it.

topics.label: read the ground he won't walk
topics.say: You see it before he says it: no path worn toward the doorstone, not even his. Whatever kept people off this mound outlasted the reason for it.

fl_sump_camp_coth.name: Coth
fl_sump_camp_coth.desc: A recruiting picket at the stakes, cloak pinned tight against the sump's damp, tally-stick tapping his own knee.

topics.label: why he's posted at the stakes
topics.say: Coth. Sergeant's got me on the stakes till the tally's done. Recruiting's slow work in a hold this empty, slower still if you're not here to sign.

topics.label: ask what the tally's counting
topics.say: He gives it up slower than the rounds did: fewer names than Coel wants, and every one of them a returner, not a recruit.

topics.label: trade a soldier's read on the stakes
topics.say: He straightens without meaning to when you talk terrain like it's yours to judge too. "Fair point," he allows, and fixes the gap you named.

fl_walker.name: fallow-walker
fl_walker.desc: Upright the way nothing lying down that long should still manage, moving with the same patient wrongness as everything else this ground grew.
onDeath: It goes down and stays down, folding back into the reed like it was never anything more than ground pretending otherwise.

fl_cur.name: a lean cur
fl_cur.desc: Ribs showing, one ear torn, watching the quarry's rim like it half-expects the ground to give up more than water.
onDeath: It goes down fast, more starved than fierce. There was never much fight in it, only hunger.

fl_wren.name: Wren
fl_wren.desc: A returner kneeling at one of the newer cairns, straightening stones that don't need straightening.

topics.label: who she's here for
topics.say: My uncle. He made it back before the ground took him too. At least he's under a stone I chose, not a furrow I didn't.

topics.label: sit with her a while
topics.say: She doesn't ask you to talk, and you don't. It's the kind of quiet that isn't empty.

topics.label: tell her plainly it gets easier
topics.say: "Does it," she says, not quite a question, and goes back to the stones. It isn't unkindness. It's just not yet.

topics.label: leave her to it, unremarked
topics.say: She doesn't look up. Whatever she needed from that, it wasn't company.
